title: Learning as Reasoning Unfolds: Progressive Rollout Allocation for Efficient Reinforcement Learning (VIGOR)
objective: policy improvement (gradient signal) under binary verifiable reward
spread_rule: greedy: extra rollouts to top-alpha prompts by observed group reward variance (x2 per round)
evidence: Abstract: iteratively allocates additional rollouts to those with the highest group reward variance
notes: Zero-variance prompts after 2 pilot rollouts get nothing more (Sec 4.2: receive no further rollout generation). Hopeless prompts discounted.

title: Spend Your Rollouts Where It Counts: Rollout Allocation for Group-Based RL Post-Training (Pilot-Commit)
objective: policy improvement (gradient signal) under binary verifiable reward
spread_rule: pilot estimate of reward variance; remaining budget to high-variance prompts, low-signal skipped
evidence: Abstract: pilot stage estimates per-prompt informativeness using a fraction of the budget

title: Cross-Epoch Adaptive Rollout Optimization for RL Post-Training (CERO)
objective: policy improvement (gradient signal) under binary verifiable reward
spread_rule: concave saturating utility from Beta-posterior expected Bernoulli variance; dual online allocation
evidence: Abstract: online resource allocation with prompt-level diminishing returns
notes: Closest to explicit marginal-value (water-filling) allocation in RL rollouts.

title: Early Verdicts, Better Budgets: Sequential Adaptive Rollout Allocation for Compute-Efficient RLVR (SARA)
objective: policy improvement (gradient signal) under binary verifiable reward
spread_rule: SPRT two-threshold: commit effective groups, abandon saturated (all-0 or all-1) after probe
evidence: Abstract: abandons saturated ones after a short probe
notes: Abandoning all-wrong groups = explicit discount of hopeless prompts.

title: Kalman Meets Curriculum: Efficient Dynamic Prompt Selection for Adaptive RL Finetuning (KGPS)
objective: policy improvement (gradient signal) under binary verifiable reward
evidence: Abstract: posterior-expected training utility that favors intermediate-difficulty prompts
notes: Signal comes free from past training rollouts (no extra rollouts).

title: Prompt Replay: Speeding up GRPO with On-Policy Reuse of High-Signal Prompts
unit: prompt reuse slots in training batches
objective: policy improvement (gradient signal) under binary verifiable reward
evidence: Abstract: prioritize prompts closer to a pass rate of 0.5
notes: Reports plateau/convergence with baseline; honest negative.

title: Beyond Normalization: Rethinking the Partition Function as a Difficulty Scheduler for RLVR (PACED-RL)
objective: policy improvement (gradient signal) under binary verifiable reward
evidence: Sec 4.3: select questions whose estimated accuracies are closest to the target accuracy
notes: target tau=0.5

title: ThinkPrior: Zero-Rollout Difficulty Priors for Cold-Start Prompt Selection in RLVR
objective: policy improvement (gradient signal) under binary verifiable reward
evidence: Abstract: selects by expected learnability and then updates from training outcomes
notes: Reports fixed-budget result as reallocation not net saving; offline anchor pass not on target budget.

title: Can Prompt Difficulty be Online Predicted for Accelerating RL Finetuning of Reasoning Models? (MoPPS)
objective: policy improvement (gradient signal) under binary verifiable reward
evidence: Abstract: models each prompt's success rate as a latent variable
notes: Thompson-sampled Beta posterior; prioritizes success rates near 0.5.

title: DAPO: An Open-Source LLM Reinforcement Learning System at Scale
objective: policy improvement (gradient signal) under binary verifiable reward
evidence: Dynamic sampling: over-sample and filter out prompts with accuracy 1 and 0
notes: Ablations by training step; discarded oversampled rollouts not charged (later papers e.g. Pilot-Commit, SARA, KGPS quantify the overhead).

title: Optimizing Chain-of-Thought Reasoners via Gradient Variance Minimization in Rejection Sampling and RL (GVM-RAFT)
objective: minimize stochastic gradient variance under compute budget
spread_rule: n_i prop. to G_i/sqrt(p_i + alpha/p_i^(beta-1)); Neyman-type (SD of per-prompt estimator)
evidence: Prop. 1: a regularization term that penalizes sampling on such prompts
notes: Without regularizer would be MONO-UP 1/sqrt(p); regularizer discounts very-low-p prompts. Estimation framing (alpha=1).

title: Act Only When It Pays: Efficient Reinforcement Learning for LLM Reasoning via Selective Rollouts (GRESO)
objective: policy improvement (gradient signal) under binary verifiable reward
evidence: Abstract: predicts and skips uninformative prompts using reward training dynamics
notes: Skips prompts zero-variance in prior epochs (both all-correct and all-wrong).

title: Online Difficulty Filtering for Reasoning Oriented Reinforcement Learning
objective: policy improvement (gradient signal) under binary verifiable reward
evidence: Abstract: selecting tasks of intermediate difficulty maximizes learning efficiency
notes: Keeps 0.3<p<0.7; compared mainly at matched gradient steps; Sec 6.2 notes aggressive filtering needs many more rollouts.

title: Self-Evolving Curriculum for LLM Reasoning (SEC)
objective: policy improvement (gradient signal) under binary verifiable reward
evidence: Abstract: absolute advantage ... as a proxy measure for immediate learning gain
notes: Bandit over categories with learning-gain reward; implicitly non-monotone.

title: Efficient Reinforcement Finetuning via Adaptive Curriculum Learning (AdaRFT)
objective: policy improvement (gradient signal) under binary verifiable reward
evidence: Abstract: trains on tasks that are challenging but solvable
notes: Target difficulty adjusted from recent reward; needs difficulty annotations.

title: VCRL: Variance-based Curriculum Reinforcement Learning for Large Language Models
objective: policy improvement (gradient signal) under binary verifiable reward
evidence: Abstract: too easy or too difficult have a lower variance

title: Reinforce-Ada: An Adaptive Sampling Framework under Non-linear RL Objectives
objective: non-linear (log-likelihood) RL objective
spread_rule: budget prop. to 1/sqrt(p_hat) (Ada-Est); sequential sample-until-K-pos/neg, Nmax=32 (Ada-Seq)
evidence: Sec 3.2: difficult prompts (low p_i) receive more samples
notes: Bayesian prior keeps zero-success prompts non-zero; only Nmax cap; Ada-Seq inference cost 2.2-2.8x GRPO (Table 3) though abstract claims same total budget.

title: Improving Sampling Efficiency in RLVR through Adaptive Rollout and Response Reuse (AR3PO)
objective: policy improvement (gradient signal) under binary verifiable reward
spread_rule: staged: prompts with a correct response exit; unsolved prompts continue to cap (8)
evidence: Abstract: dynamically allocates more responses to difficult prompts
notes: Pure first-success rule; unsolved-after-cap prompts get full budget plus a reused old correct response.

title: Improving Data Efficiency for LLM Reinforcement Fine-tuning Through Difficulty-targeted Online Data Selection and Rollout Replay (DOTS)
objective: policy improvement (gradient signal) under binary verifiable reward
evidence: Abstract: prioritizing questions of moderate difficulty
notes: Reference-set rollouts used for attention-based difficulty prediction.

title: Learning to Reason at the Frontier of Learnability (LILO)
objective: policy improvement (gradient signal) under binary verifiable reward
evidence: Abstract: prioritises questions with high variance of success
notes: Cost of learnability evaluation not verified (full text fetch failed).

title: CurES: From Gradient Analysis to Efficient Curriculum Learning for Reasoning LLMs
unit: prompt sampling probability + rollouts per prompt
objective: gradient convergence / variance
spread_rule: rollouts n_i prop. to sigma_i (Neyman, SD); prompt sampling prop. to exp(sqrt(p(1-p))/tau)
evidence: Sec 5.2: prompts of intermediate accuracy allocated more rollout quantities
notes: Neyman-correct for gradient estimation; Bayesian posterior to cut estimation cost.

title: Depth-Breadth Synergy in RLVR: Unlocking LLM Reasoning Gains with Adaptive Exploration (DARS)
objective: Pass@K / cumulative advantage
spread_rule: Hardness-weighted: extra rollouts scale with 1 - acc, capped at N_max
evidence: Abstract: re-weights difficult problems by using targeted, multi-stage rollouts
notes: Zero-accuracy problems get maximum extra rollouts (Sec 3.1 HW schedule); pre-rollout pass to estimate acc.

title: XRPO: Pushing the limits of GRPO with Targeted Exploration and Exploitation
objective: policy improvement (gradient signal) under binary verifiable reward
spread_rule: priority = expected CI half-width reduction (prop. to s_q) + UCB bonus
evidence: Abstract: adaptively prioritizes prompts with higher potential for uncertainty reduction
notes: Zero-accuracy prompts handled by ICL seeding rather than more rollouts.

title: Kimi k1.5: Scaling Reinforcement Learning with LLMs
objective: policy improvement (gradient signal) under binary verifiable reward
evidence: Sec 2.3.4: sample problems proportional to 1-s_i
notes: Prioritized sampling itself not ablated vs uniform (only curriculum sampling is); weak inclusion.

title: Prompt Curriculum Learning for Efficient LLM Post-Training (PCL)
objective: policy improvement (gradient signal) under binary verifiable reward
evidence: Abstract: selects intermediate-difficulty prompts using a learned value model

title: Hard Examples Are All You Need: Maximizing GRPO Post-Training Under Annotation Budgets
objective: post-GRPO accuracy
evidence: Abstract: Training on the hardest 10% of examples
notes: Counterpoint: MONO-UP wins vs easy/random here, since hard set still has mixed outcomes; difficulty estimated with base-model samples not charged.

title: DUET: Optimize Token-Budget Allocation for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
objective: gradient variance / accuracy at token budget
spread_rule: cost-weighted Neyman n_q prop. to sigma_q/sqrt(L_q)
evidence: Sec 3.1: cost-weighted Neyman rule
notes: Explicitly invokes Neyman allocation.

title: Not All Rollouts are Useful: Down-Sampling Rollouts in LLM Reinforcement Learning (PODS)
exclude_reason: within-prompt rollout down-sampling for update; no across-prompt allocation
